items.title: Infostealers In Banking Fraud: How Stolen Credentials Lead To Silent Intrusions
items.summary: Infostealers enable banking fraud: one stolen log feeds four crimes, hides in the stage no team owns, and moves weeks before any transaction fires.

items.title: From Streaming to Stealing: Mirax and the Rise of Server-side Android Device Takeover in META
items.summary: Discover how the Mirax Android malware campaign uses streaming app lures, server-side C2, and Accessibility Service abuse for device takeover targeting financial institutions in the META region.

items.title: Deepfake Fraud Prevention: Why Detection Alone Fails
items.summary: Deepfake fraud kits sell for $5. Learn how it reaches enterprises, real cases Group-IB investigated, and why detection alone can’t stop it.

items.title: MadApe: The Code That Opens the Door
items.summary: Group-IB uncovers MadApe, a previously undocumented Microsoft Device Code phishing kit that uses business-themed PDF lures, configurable redirects and fake document-sharing pages to trick victims into completing Microsoft Device Code authentication across a broad infrastructure cluster.

items.title: Frost Radar 2026: Enterprise Risk and Path to Preemptive Security
items.summary: Why connecting exposure, adversary intelligence, and response should help organizations intervene earlier.

items.title: False Protection, Emptied Accounts: The Seven Android Trojan Families Targeting Indian Banking Apps
items.summary: This technical analysis details a sophisticated Android malware campaign targeting the Indian banking sector. The report examines seven distinct trojan families that facilitate banking fraud through coordinated phishing, credential theft, and unauthorized cryptojacking. Group-IB provides an in-depth breakdown of the attack chain, malware capabilities, and the infrastructure used to compromise mobile devices.

items.title: Inside SiriusQT: A Seriously Skilled RAT
Stray Cat, Open Doors: How k0t Wanders Through the Network Edge
items.summary: Group-IB and NyxLab expose threat actor k0t's large-scale campaign exploiting FortiGate, FortiWeb, and Palo Alto GlobalProtect edge devices to harvest credentials, establish persistent access and exfiltrate data

items.title: The Checker You Pay For
items.summary: How criminals turn spend-management onboarding into fraud infrastructure, and why you may be accountable for the fraud you never see.

items.title: KGB RAT: A Fully Undetectable Windows Trojan Built to Spy, Steal, and Terrorize
items.summary: Group-IB researchers analyze KGB RAT, a Windows Remote Access Trojan advertised on underground forums as being fully undetectable, featuring a built-in crypter, HVNC, credential theft, ransomware, and an unusual set of psychological harassment capabilities.

items.title: Agentic AI In Cybersecurity: What Changes When The System Chooses The Next Step
items.summary: Agentic AI is the breakthrough of the moment, in security as everywhere else: agents that are threat-aware, active, and proactive in investigation.  But it is also the technology behind a recent documented autonomous AI intrusion. Both facts are true, and the distance between them is what this article is about.

items.title: From Detonation to Detection: The Sandbox Now Writes the Rules
items.summary: Understanding what a malware sample does and being able to detect it are two different jobs, and the second one needs a skill many teams are short of. The Group-IB Malware Detonation Platform now produces indicators, Sigma rules, and hunting queries from the behavior it observes.

items.title: Anatomía de BraZetsu: Cómo los cibercriminales abastecen el ecosistema clandestino
items.summary: Group-IB descubre BraZetsu, un nuevo malware para Windows basado en Python que funciona como un toolkit maestro para Initial Access Brokers y potencia un marketplace clandestino único, mejorado con IA, para comercializar objetivos comprometidos en Iberoamérica y Latinoamérica.

items.title: Milk Dragon: Huge Discounts on Social Media? Think Twice Before You Buy
items.summary: Milk Dragon, also known as NaiLong is an Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing kit active since October 2025. Unlike conventional phishing tactics that rely on fear and urgency, Milk Dragon lures victims with big discounts on consumer goods distributed via Facebook and TikTok marketplace advertisements.

items.title: No One Gets Phished: The New Group-IB Browser Agent Applies Predictive Intelligence At The Click
items.summary: One employee reaches a phishing page. The tab closes, the domain is blocked for every browser in the company, and the targeted password is already being reset. The new Group-IB Browser Agent brings the corporate browser under XDR coverage, checking every page against predictive Threat Intelligence in real time.

items.title: RemControl: AI Built the Overlays. Victims Lose their PINs
items.summary: Group-IB uncovers RemControl, a new Android banking trojan targeting European, Middle Eastern and Canadian banks, whose criminal infrastructure was unknowingly built by AI.

items.title: HEAVYGRAM: A Telegram-based Surveillance Backdoor Linked to Handala Hack
items.summary: Group-IB Threat Intelligence analyzes HEAVYGRAM, a Telegram-based Windows backdoor attributed with moderate confidence to the Iran-linked threat actor Handala Hack. Active since Fall 2023, it has been used to surveil Iranian dissidents, journalists and government opponents, enabling remote command execution, data exfiltration, and persistence over Telegram command-and-control.

items.title: Top 5 Fraud Prevention Platforms for Banks and Fintechs in 2026
items.summary: Most fraud platforms only see a threat once it becomes a transaction. This guide compares the top 5 fraud prevention platforms for banks and fintechs in 2026, including Group-IB, Feedzai, Sift, DataVisor, and Kount, and what actually separates them.

items.title: The Adversary We Are Fighting Is Now a Full-Force Industry: Inside cybercrime’s new economy
items.summary: Attacks now are cheap, fast, and outsourced. The recent research shows what it changes and how organizations should strategy defense.

items.title: Smish. Click. Drained: Inside the Smishing Triad’s Phishing Cockpit
items.summary: A deep technical analysis of the Smishing Triad’s JWR phishing kit and Outsider operator cluster, revealing its real-time victim control, encrypted WebSocket communications, multi-stage credential theft, AES-256-CTR implementation, infrastructure, and actionable indicators for defenders.

items.title: Vwork: Weaponized Open-source Software as an Addon for Gigabud
items.summary: How the Gigabud Android banking trojan abuses Shelter, an open-source app cloner, and what that means for banks, users, and defenders.

items.title: Ransomware in 2026: What the Data Demands From You
items.summary: Group-IB's 2026 data shows ransomware accelerating across APAC. See where response plans fail, and the 5-pillar framework built to hold under pressure.

items.title: One Adversary: The 90-Day Fusion Playbook
items.summary: Fusion is a capability you mature into, not a team you hire. Here is the honest maturity path, the metrics that fund it, and the on-ramp that costs no headcount, startable this quarter.

items.title: The Outsider Phishing Kit: A Resilient Threat in the Face of Law Enforcement Action
items.summary: This blog provides a deep-dive into the phishing kit created by Chenlun known as the Outsider Phishing Kit. It is a well established kit in the Chinese community with over 267 ready-made phishing templates targeting over 54 countries worldwide.

items.title: Anatomy of BraZetsu: How Cybercriminals Fuel the Underground Ecosystem
items.summary: Group-IB uncovers BraZetsu, a new Python-based Windows malware that serves as a master toolkit for Initial Access Brokers and powers a unique, AI-enhanced underground marketplace for commercializing compromised Iberian and Latin American targets.

items.title: One Adversary, Two Outcomes: The 0.027% Proof
items.summary: One malware campaign, 11,000 compromised devices, two banks with very different outcomes. At the bank with fused defence, fraud succeeded on just 0.027% of compromised devices; nine times less than the market average. Regulators are taking notice too.

items.title: Tortoiseshell: New Toolset and Operational Infrastructure Exposed
items.summary: Group-IB Threat Intelligence performed enrichment and APT hunting based on recent public data about the Tortoiseshell APT group, leading to the discovery of new samples sharing similarities with known Tortoiseshell malware and additional operational infrastructure.

items.title: Balonx Sistema: El Rostro Detrás del PhaaS que Impacta la Banca Mexicana
items.summary: Group-IB expone una operación mexicana de PhaaS dirigida a más de 20 instituciones financieras, con capacidades de phishing en tiempo real, vishing con IA y RAT para dispositivos móviles.

items.title: One Adversary: Fraud Is a Network, Not a Payment
items.summary: Payment was authorised. The transaction was, technically, legitimate. It was also part of a $187 million criminal network, and the payment was the worst place to fight it.

items.title: Balonx Sistema: The Face Behind the PhaaS Affecting Mexican Banking
items.summary: Group-IB exposes a Mexican PhaaS operation targeting over 20 financial institutions with live phishing, AI vishing, and mobile RAT capabilities.
